questions.question: Which statement correctly defines mass?
options: The gravitational force acting on an object
The volume occupied by a substance
A measure of the amount of matter in a body
The weight of an object divided by gravitational field strength
questions.explanation: Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in a body. It is a scalar quantity measured in kilograms (kg) and does not change with location.

questions.question: An object has a mass of 8 kg on Earth. What is its mass on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property of matter and does not change with location. The object's mass remains 8 kg on the Moon, although its weight would be different due to the Moon's weaker gravitational field.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes between mass and weight?
options: Mass is measured in newtons; weight is measured in kilograms
Mass changes with location; weight is constant everywhere
Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the gravitational force on that mass
Mass is a vector; weight is a scalar quantity
questions.explanation: Mass measures the amount of matter (kg, scalar, constant). Weight is the gravitational force acting on that mass (N, vector, varies with g). Relationship: W = mg.

questions.question: A box has a mass of 15 kg. What is its weight on Earth where g = 10 N/kg?
questions.explanation: Using W = mg: Weight = 15 kg × 10 N/kg = 150 N. Weight is the gravitational force acting on the mass.

questions.question: What is the definition of gravitational field strength, g?
options: The force per unit area acting on a surface
The gravitational force per unit mass placed at a point
The acceleration of an object in free fall only
The weight of an object multiplied by its mass
questions.explanation: Gravitational field strength, g, is defined as the gravitational force per unit mass placed at that point. On Earth's surface, g ≈ 10 N/kg or 10 m/s².

questions.question: A block of metal has a mass of 360 g and a volume of 45 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Using ρ = m/V: Density = 360 g ÷ 45 cm³ = 8 g/cm³. Density is mass per unit volume.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect the pressure exerted by a solid object on a surface?
options: The force applied by the object
The area of contact between object and surface
questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as force per unit area (P = F/A). It depends on the force (often weight) and contact area. The colour of the object has no effect on pressure.

questions.explanation: Minimum pressure occurs on the largest face: Area = 10 cm × 5 cm = 50 cm² = 0.005 m². Weight = mg = 0.5 kg × 10 N/kg = 5 N. P = F/A = 5 N ÷ 0.005 m² = 1000 Pa. questions.question: Why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a blunt knife?
options: The sharp knife has less mass
The sharp knife is made of a denser material
The sharp knife applies the same force over a smaller area, increasing pressure
The sharp knife has a larger surface area in contact with the object
questions.explanation: Pressure P = F/A. A sharp knife has a very small contact area at the edge. For the same applied force, this results in much higher pressure, allowing it to cut through materials more easily.

questions.question: Why do buildings have wide foundations?
options: To increase the weight of the building
To decrease the pressure on the ground by increasing the contact area
To make the building look more stable
To reduce the density of the building materials
questions.explanation: Pressure P = F/A. Wide foundations increase the contact area (A) with the ground. For the same weight (force F), this reduces the pressure exerted on the ground, preventing sinking.

questions.question: A liquid has a density of 0.9 g/cm³. What is the mass of 200 cm³ of this liquid?
questions.explanation: Using m = ρV: Mass = 0.9 g/cm³ × 200 cm³ = 180 g. Density relates mass and volume.

questions.question: An astronaut has a weight of 700 N on Earth (g = 10 N/kg). What would be their mass on Mars where g = 3.7 N/kg?
questions.explanation: Mass is constant regardless of location. First find mass on Earth: m = W/g = 700 N ÷ 10 N/kg = 70 kg. This mass remains 70 kg on Mars, although weight would change.

questions.question: Which statement about pressure is CORRECT?
options: Pressure increases when area increases for the same force
Pressure decreases when force decreases for the same area
questions.explanation: Pressure P = F/A. If force decreases while area stays constant, pressure decreases. Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa = N/m²) and is a scalar quantity.

questions.question: A cube of side 2 cm has a mass of 64 g. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Volume of cube = side³ = 2 cm × 2 cm × 2 cm = 8 cm³. Using ρ = m/V: Density = 64 g ÷ 8 cm³ = 8 g/cm³.
